question: Dortmund Airport has submitted a complaint to the Commission stating that it has been put at a competitive disadvantage as a result of the aid granted by the German Government to other German airports as compensation for revenue losses incurred during the COVID-19 crisis in 2020. 1.

When will a decision be made regarding the complaint submitted by Dortmund Airport on 14 January 2022 (registration number comp(2022)312595) that was last addressed by the Commission in a letter dated 25 October 2023?
Are there any other pending proceedings concerning COVID-19 related aid for airports in the EU, and if so, what are they?
What is the average length of proceedings for comparable aid procedures, and how has this figure changed in recent years?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2024) 1. On 11 August 2020 the Commission approved a German aid scheme to support airports affected by the COVID-19 pandemic that allowed German authorities at different levels (federal, state and municipal) to compensate airports for revenue losses caused by the pandemic. The scheme contains objective criteria that airports must meet to be eligible for aid.

As the Court of Justice has recognised1, Member States are not obliged to grant aid to all companies active in a sector but may reserve that aid to a limited number of companies. On 25 October 2023 and 11 June 2024, the Directorate-General for Competition informed the complainant that there is no duty to grant aid to all operators in a sector and recommended it to revert to the German authorities. 2.

There is one pending procedure relating to an airport in the context of aid related to the COVID-19 pandemic. That case is not comparable with the one about which the Honourable Member. 3. Member States may notify or pre-notify their State aid projects at any stage in the design of such planned measures, which makes it difficult to extract meaningful information from the average length of State aid procedures.

When the Member State notifies a planned measure that is sufficiently mature and designed to comply with State aid rules, the Commission can take a decision rapidly. Other planned measures that are less mature require shaping or redesign to bring them into line with State aid rules.
1 Judgement of 28 September 2023 in case C-320/21 P, Ryanair v Commission (SAS, Sweden; Covid-19),
